solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Mean to be ready to fight

definitions.meaning: mean here is stingy, unwilling to part with money
read literally, with hands clenched into fists, set for a punch-up

explanation.walkthrough: The second sense takes the compound word literally: fists held tight, about to throw a punch. 'to be' just joins the two definitions.
explanation.definitionFit: A miser keeps a tight grip on cash, so the idiom for stingy is a synonym of mean.

clue.text: Meeting turns out to be full

indicators.note: turns out means the letters are turned into a new pattern

explanation.surface: The meeting proves to be packed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'turns out' looks like 'proves'; it rearranges MEETING.
explanation.definitionFit: Teeming means swarming or crammed, so full of people or things.

clue.text: The game's up! Edward's confined to school

indicators.note: in a down entry, up says the word is written bottom to top

parts.note: tag is a children's chasing game; the 's is the verb is
Ed is the short form of Edward

explanation.surface: A pupil caught and kept in at school: the game is up.
explanation.walkthrough: 'up' reverses the game, as suits a down entry. Gated is British boarding-school slang for kept inside the grounds as a punishment.
explanation.definitionFit: In public-school slang a gated pupil is forbidden to leave school grounds, kept confined.

clue.text: Staff of police

parts.note: staff seems to mean the personnel of a police force, but it is a stick carried by them

explanation.walkthrough: Staff suggests employees; it is the wooden club a constable carries.
explanation.definitionFit: A short club carried by a British police officer is a staff in the sense of a stick.

clue.text: One at the front is terrible Russian leader

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral for one
the van, short for vanguard, is the front of an army

explanation.surface: Whoever is out in front is a dreadful Russian ruler.
explanation.walkthrough: Ivan the Terrible was the sixteenth-century tsar of Russia.
explanation.definitionFit: Ivan IV, known as the Terrible, was the first tsar to rule Russia.

clue.text: American music of the Depression?

parts.note: suggests a style from the 1930s slump, but means music expressing low spirits

explanation.walkthrough: The capital D points to the Great Depression; the musical genre is about depression of mood.
explanation.definitionFit: A melancholy African-American song form takes its name from a word for low spirits.

clue.text: A bloomer, I'd say, in a way

indicators.note: in a way hints that the words are arranged in another fashion

explanation.surface: Someone admits that, in a manner of speaking, a mistake was made.
explanation.walkthrough: 'A bloomer' looks like a blunder, but is a flowering plant; 'in a way' rearranges I'D SAY.
explanation.definitionFit: A daisy is a flower, something that blooms, so literally a bloomer.

clue.text: Irritated when necessity took first place

parts.note: a need is a necessity
led means was at the front, took first place

explanation.surface: Someone was annoyed when need won out.
explanation.definitionFit: Needled means provoked or annoyed, a synonym of irritated.

clue.text: Went and got married again

definitions.meaning: as in retiring to another room: went off somewhere
read as ..., paired off once more

explanation.walkthrough: The first sense is the formal verb for withdrawing somewhere; the second splits the word as re-paired.
explanation.definitionFit: To repair to a place is a formal way of saying to go there.

clue.text: Train from Eton, perhaps, going to university at right time

indicators.note: perhaps suggests the school's name might be arranged some other way

parts.note: an age is a long period of time

explanation.surface: A train of followers sets out from Eton for university at the proper moment.
explanation.walkthrough: 'perhaps' rearranges the school's name. Train here is a retinue of followers, not a railway carriage.
explanation.definitionFit: A train can be a body of attendants following an important person, which is a retinue.

clue.text: Girl providing passion to one lacking love

parts.note: ire is anger, a fierce passion

indicators.note: lacking says the word one goes without something

parts.note: taken as written
love is zero in tennis, shaped like the letter O

explanation.surface: A girl brings passion to someone who has no love in their life.
explanation.walkthrough: Love as the letter O comes from tennis scoring; 'lacking' removes it.
explanation.definitionFit: Irene is a female first name, so it is an example of a girl.

clue.text: Prompt delivery

definitions.meaning: to prompt is to bring about or persuade, a verb
here a hint at childbirth: doctors may bring on labour artificially to start the delivery

explanation.walkthrough: The second definition is loose: the verb means bringing on a birth artificially, which the clue compresses to 'delivery'.
explanation.definitionFit: To prompt someone to act is to persuade or cause them to, the general verb sense.

clue.text: Co-operate to meet delivery

definitions.meaning: to co-operate is to go along with others' plans
in cricket or baseball, the call to start play, when the batter faces the bowled ball

explanation.walkthrough: The idiom for joining in also literally means engaging with a ball sent down to you.
explanation.definitionFit: Going along with others is the informal idiom for co-operating.

clue.text: Last resting places for wine

definitions.meaning: a wine from the Bordeaux district of France, red or white

explanation.definitionFit: Burial plots are the final resting places of the dead.

clue.text: Landing place advertises tour

parts.note: to air something is to make it public
a trip is a journey or tour

explanation.surface: A landing spot promotes a holiday excursion.
explanation.definitionFit: A strip of ground for planes to take off and land is a landing place.

clue.text: Blamed the head chef before having made certain

indicators.note: the head of the chef is its first letter

parts.note: to ensure is to make certain

explanation.surface: The head chef was blamed for having made certain of something.
explanation.walkthrough: 'head' looks like part of a job title, head chef, but it takes the first letter C.
explanation.definitionFit: Censured means formally criticised, a synonym of blamed.

clue.text: Drink now mixed in separate container

indicators.note: in places the rearranged letters within the word for separate

parts.note: to sunder is to split apart

indicators.note: mixed says the word now is jumbled

explanation.surface: A drink is now blended inside a divided vessel.
explanation.walkthrough: 'mixed' scrambles the second word and 'in' sets it inside the word for separate; 'container' only reinforces that. A sundowner is an evening drink.
explanation.definitionFit: A sundowner is an alcoholic drink taken around sunset.

clue.text: Reproduction of a man's oil painting

indicators.note: reproduction suggests a copy, but here the letters are recombined

explanation.surface: A print of a male portrait in oils.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Reproduction of' rearranges A MAN'S OIL, counting the S.
explanation.definitionFit: Leonardo's portrait in the Louvre is perhaps the most famous painting in the world.

clue.text: Switches on for one daily period

indicators.note: switches means the letters are swapped around into a new order

explanation.surface: Turning the lights on for one particular part of each day.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Switches' looks like light switches; it rearranges ON FOR ONE.
explanation.definitionFit: The morning, before midday, is a period that comes round every day.

clue.text: New-fangled sort of wheel

indicators.note: new says the letters take a fresh form

explanation.surface: A newfangled design of wheel.
explanation.walkthrough: The hyphen splits 'New-fangled': 'New' rearranges FANGLED.
explanation.definitionFit: A train wheel has a projecting rim to keep it on the rail, so it is a flanged kind.

clue.text: A poem's positive points

parts.note: an is the form of a before a vowel
an ode is a poem; with the 's it gives the plural form

explanation.surface: A poem has upbeat, positive features.
explanation.walkthrough: Read as 'an ode's'. In electrolysis the anode is the positive electrode.
explanation.definitionFit: Anodes are positive electrodes, the terminals where current enters a cell.

clue.text: Just one type of shirt or vest

parts.note: single means only one
a T-shirt is a type of shirt, giving the letter T

explanation.surface: Only one kind of shirt or vest.
explanation.definitionFit: A singlet is a sleeveless vest, the British word for an undershirt.

clue.text: Before embracing, Anne put out feelers

indicators.note: embracing means the word for before holds something inside

parts.note: ante is Latin for before, as in ante-room

indicators.note: put out signals the name is disturbed into another order

explanation.surface: Before a hug, Anne tentatively reached out.
explanation.walkthrough: 'put out' scrambles the name and 'embracing' wraps the Latin word for before around it.
explanation.definitionFit: Antennae are an insect's sensory organs, feelers in a literal sense.

clue.text: Wants to be seen holding a number up

indicators.note: in a down entry, up means the result is read from bottom to top
holding says one word contains the other

parts.note: D is the Roman numeral for 500

explanation.surface: Someone wants to be spotted with a number held aloft.
explanation.walkthrough: 'holding' makes SDEEN; 'up' reverses it.
explanation.definitionFit: Needs and wants are both things a person requires, a direct synonym.

clue.text: I snoop around to discover a cause of death

indicators.note: around suggests the letters are moved about

explanation.surface: A detective poking around to uncover how someone died.
explanation.walkthrough: 'around' rearranges I SNOOP.
explanation.definitionFit: Toxic substances kill when taken, making them an example of a lethal agent.

clue.text: A gesture one doesn't care to make

definitions.text: A gesture one doesn't care to make

parts.words: A gesture one doesn't care to make
parts.note: seems to mean an unwelcome gesture, but means one made to show you do not care

explanation.walkthrough: 'doesn't care to make' reads as reluctance; it is the shoulder movement of indifference.
explanation.definitionFit: Lifting the shoulders is the body's way of signalling indifference.

clue.text: Look round to leg perhaps

parts.note: O is round in shape

indicators.note: perhaps hints the word leg could be arranged otherwise

explanation.surface: Glancing towards the leg side in cricket.
explanation.walkthrough: 'perhaps' rearranges LEG to GLE. 'Leg' is also the cricket field's leg side.
explanation.definitionFit: To ogle is to look at someone lecherously, a kind of looking.

clue.text: Dirt, for example, returns round the edge

indicators.note: round says the reversed letters go about the next piece
returns says the abbreviation is turned back to front

parts.note: e.g. abbreviates exempli gratia, for example
a rim is the edge of something

explanation.surface: Dirt, for instance, comes back around the rim of something.
explanation.walkthrough: 'returns' turns the abbreviation backwards and 'round' sets it outside the word for edge.
explanation.definitionFit: Grime is ingrained dirt, a direct synonym.

clue.text: Widely seen as a popular army officer

parts.note: in means fashionable or popular
a general is a senior army officer

explanation.surface: A well-liked army officer is broadly regarded so.
explanation.definitionFit: Speaking generally means taking the wide or overall view, a synonym of widely.

clue.text: Ongoing panic

parts.note: read ongoing as on-going, the fear an actor feels about going on in front of an audience

explanation.walkthrough: 'Ongoing' usually means continuing; split it as going on, and it is a performer about to go on.
explanation.definitionFit: Nerves felt before performing are the panic of going onstage.
